question.prompt: The three-pair budget cut deferred the scenario that would prove a title chosen from the `Recently published` section opens that same book's detail page. How should this deferred route be handled in a later rework?

options.label: Raise budget
options.detail: Increase the pair budget above 3 and add the deferred recent-book route with its own test.

options.label: Swap coverage
options.detail: Replace a lower-priority kept scenario with the deferred recent-book route if sampled-book navigation matters more than one current branch.

options.label: Accept deferral
options.detail: Leave this route uncovered for now and rely on the gap until a later assurance pass.

content.risk_rationale: Deferring this route leaves the home page's sampled-book navigation unproven even though the source promises that each recently published title links to that book's detail page. The risk is moderate because the use-case still retains coverage for both explicit primary branch CTAs under the current budget.

content.title: Review the home page discovery content and section counts
content.intent: Prove that the home page presents the discovery content promised to a first-time visitor: the heading, the catalog-size statement, four package previews with their required metadata, and four recently published book tiles.
content.technique_notes: Applied source-grounded happy-path coverage and equivalence partitioning to the single anonymous landing state. No boundary, negative, or covering-array expansion applied because the home page in REQ-02 exposes no user input, numeric control, or outcome-changing combinations on this path. Budget rank 1/4 because this one journey exercises most public discovery content on the page.

content.title: Use the publishing CTAs on the home page to reach the packages page
content.intent: Prove that each home-page publishing call to action that promises the publishing packages page takes the visitor to `/publish`.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the two publishing controls with the same promised outcome: `Start Publishing` and `Compare all packages →`. Kept as one scenario with equivalent-control variation because the outcome does not change. No covering-array expansion applied because there is only one equivalence family on this path. Budget rank 2/4 because these CTAs are primary public conversion routes into the author flow.

content.title: Use the catalog CTA on the home page to reach the published books catalog
content.intent: Prove that the home-page CTA for browsing all published books takes the visitor to `/books`.
content.technique_notes: Applied source-grounded happy-path coverage to the explicit catalog outbound route. Kept separate from the recently published title route because the outcomes differ: this path must land on `/books`, while a recent-book title must land on a specific book detail page. Budget rank 3/4 because it covers one of the use-case's named public branch choices.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Scored highest because a single landing-page review covers the fixed public content that every visitor sees: heading, catalog-size claim, package-preview structure, and recent-books count.
[value_score] Scored second because broken publishing CTAs would misroute prospective authors at the first public conversion point, affecting the publishing half of the platform directly.
[value_score] Scored third because the catalog CTA is one of the use-case's named outbound choices and is the cleanest route into the book-browsing half of the platform.

[value_score] Scored fourth and was budget-evicted because it proves a narrower sampled-content route whose exact target varies with the recent-books fixture, making it less valuable than the explicit catalog CTA under a three-pair cap.
[applicability] Happy-path scenarios applied because REQ-02 describes the intended anonymous visitor journeys through a public landing page.
[applicability] No negative home-page scenario was minted because the source for REQ-02 defines no invalid input, missing-resource variant, or alternate error behavior on the home page itself.

[applicability] Boundary analysis did not apply at the scenario level because REQ-02 exposes fixed counts and text on a static public page, not an input range or paginated control with user-set bounds.

[applicability] An a11y-specific scenario was not minted in this budgeted pass because the source does not promise accessibility-only behavior unique to a separate journey; any applicable accessibility checks can still ride on kept scenarios during wiring and test design.
[applicability] No performance scenario was minted because the source states no latency or performance promise for the home page.
[applicability] No i18n scenario was minted because the source states fixed English copy but no locale-dependent behavior, formatting rule, or translation promise for the home page.
